DeepSeek just dropped dsh-superagent-prototype, a cutting-edge research harness designed for proactive, autonomous coding agents that minimize human interruption while maximizing engineering output. 🚀

Tired of acting as the constant bottleneck in AI-assisted software development? 

The new deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype solves this by providing a proactive coding agent bundle for the DeepSeek Harness architecture. It autonomously listens to events from GitHub and Feishu, evaluates requests against team-defined rules, executes tasks in isolated directories, and interacts back via pull requests and human-in-the-loop web panels only when necessary.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for AI engineers and backend leads:

⚡ DeepSeek Harness integration packaged as a proactive agent bundle for single repository management.
🔌 Event-driven automation listening to GitHub and Feishu with strict role and authorization boundaries.
🛡️ Isolated execution environments where agents handle tasks in dedicated directories and sessions.
🎛️ Human-in-the-loop web panel specifically designed to surface only items requiring manual developer attention.

Whether you want to deploy an autonomous triage and PR creation agent for your enterprise repository, or you want to study advanced agentic design patterns and safe execution architectures, this repository is an invaluable reference.

Stop getting lost in massive, unfamiliar codebases. 🗺️✨

Whether you are drowning in legacy code or trying to make sense of a massive web of AI-generated files, understanding how a system actually fits together shouldn't take weeks. 

Enter Floorplan: an open-source tool that combines LLMs like Claude and Codex with interactive visual mapping to instantly turn complex codebases into explorable, plain-English maps of your app. 🚀

Here is how it fixes the universal developer onboarding and auditing headache:

🔍 Cross-Repo & Frontend-to-Backend Mapping: Automatically matches web requests in frontend code to server endpoints across separate repositories.
🔒 Health Check Security Analysis: Identifies common AI-built app flaws like hardcoded API keys, open database tables, and unauthenticated endpoints—complete with ready-to-paste fixes.
🟢 AI-Assisted Recent Work Tracking: Lights up changed cards in green after an AI agent updates code, providing clear annotations on what was modified and why.
📋 Interactive PRD Blueprints: Generates architectural blueprints and build plans directly from product requirement documents before you even write a line of code.

Eliminate the guesswork of "vibe-coded" repositories, onboard team members in minutes, trace complex data flows visually, and catch critical security risks before shipping to production. 

Check out the repo, drop a star, and start mapping your architecture today:
https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan

Level up your low-level systems game: Eglantine has arrived as a high-performance, open-source emulator targeting next-generation console hardware, built on the architectural lineage of Yuzu and Eden! 🚀

If you are a systems engineer, graphics programmer, or reverse engineer tired of limited tooling for next-gen hardware, Eglantine solves the challenge head-on. It provides a robust, modern C++ codebase designed to run software and games intended for next-generation portable console hardware, succeeding earlier popular emulation ecosystems.

Here is what is under the hood:
⚡ Written in C++ with a strong focus on cross-platform portability across Windows, Linux, and macOS.
⚡ Derived from mature emulation codebases, inheriting a robust foundation for hardware abstraction and instruction translation.
⚡ Early-stage capability to boot and run demanding, unreleased-generation titles like Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders.
⚡ Active development tooling ecosystem and structured user documentation to onboard new reverse engineering and emulation contributors.

Why it matters for developers: 
Working on systems-level programming, hardware acceleration, JIT compilers, or graphics translation layers? You can study Eglantine's codebase to understand how next-gen console architectures are reverse-engineered and emulated. It offers a practical sandbox for learning low-level C++, memory management, and cross-platform graphics API integration.

Check out the repository and dive into the source code today:
https://github.com/Djihads80/Eglantine

Transform rigid technical documents into organic masterpieces with procedural, Lua-driven Delft-blue botanical page margins compiled directly into your LaTeX PDFs! 🌿✨

Are you tired of sterile, uniform whitespace in your technical documents, academic theses, and automated reports? Traditional publishing tools struggle to bridge the gap between rigorous document structure and organic graphic design, leaving margins awkwardly empty.

Enter Florilegium (https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium), a unique project that bridges procedural generation, graphic design, and traditional document publishing by dynamically generating algorithmic page margins, drop caps, and illustrations inside LaTeX and Typst documents using custom Lua scripts. 

Without relying on external image assets or imported vector paths, it computes parametric curves on the fly to paint watercolor-like botanical motifs, geometric lattices, or mathematical visualizations that intelligently fill empty whitespace.

Key features include:
🌱 Procedural Layout and Growth: Utilizes a greedy space-filling algorithm derived from 1998 ornament literature to dynamically grow vines, leaves, and flowers that naturally adapt to available page whitespace.
🎨 Embedded Lua Rendering: Executes custom Lua code during compilation to render parametric curves, color gradients in OKLCH color space, and organic watercolor washes straight into the output PDF.
🐝 Context-Aware Typography: Integrates directly with document elements, allowing ornaments to weave through drop-cap font counters, align with section headings, and place visitors like bees and birds.
🧩 Modular Theme System: Swap visual engines seamlessly to transition from organic Delft-blue flora to flat-shaded geometric crystals or cascading mathematical figures.

For developers and creative technologists, it demonstrates how procedural generation, mathematical layout algorithms, and embedded scripting languages can be integrated into traditional build pipelines. Use it to study advanced algorithmic layout logic, leverage custom Lua-driven rendering inside TeX engines, or adapt its concepts for automated document design and dynamic graphic assets.

Check out the repository and give it a star:
